clue.text: A regular poser, no doubt

parts.note: surface reading: someone who habitually strikes attitudes or sets puzzles
setter's reading: a person who sits for painters as a regular job

explanation.walkthrough: A poser sounds like a show-off or a tricky question; here it is literally someone who poses, regularly, for painters.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person earns a living holding still for painters, so posing is their regular occupation.

clue.text: Girl, given Chinese food, wanting more

parts.note: a girl's name
the staple of Chinese meals

explanation.surface: A girl offered a Chinese meal is still hungry for more.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed is the constant desire for more wealth or possessions, so the craving names that vice.

clue.text: An outside line to ring

parts.note: surface reading: an external telephone line
setter's reading: a straight line touching a circle from outside

explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside line' and 'ring' suggest telephoning; the ring is a circle, and the line just grazes it on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry this is a straight line meeting a circle at exactly one point without crossing inside it.

clue.text: Plan game anew after false start

indicators.note: doing something anew means making it over again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a false version is not the genuine order, so these letters are jumbled too

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: After a false start, a team rethinks its game plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams: the jumbled 'start' comes first because the game comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning scheme or ruse devised to outwit an opponent.

clue.text: French military cover

parts.note: surface reading: protection given to troops, as in covering fire
setter's reading: a tall peaked cap worn by soldiers, as in French and other armies

explanation.walkthrough: Cover here is headgear rather than protection; the cap with a plume was standard in Napoleonic-era armies.
explanation.definitionFit: This stiff cylindrical peaked cap with a plume was worn by soldiers, notably in the French army.

clue.text: Porridge going round at breakfast, say

parts.note: a round shape, the letter O
taken as written
breakfast is an example of a meal

explanation.surface: Porridge being passed round the table at breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground oats are the grain from which porridge is cooked, and the word also names the porridge itself.

clue.text: You'll probably be surprised, if it goes up

definitions.text: You'll probably be surprised, if it goes up

parts.note: surface reading: something rising, like a price or a rocket
setter's reading: the arch of hair above the eye that lifts when a face shows astonishment

explanation.walkthrough: The rising thing sounds like prices; it is the hair arch over the eye, raised in astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: People lift this facial feature involuntarily when astonished, so raising it signals surprise.

clue.text: They provide outstanding images

parts.note: surface reading: excellent pictures
setter's reading: viewers whose pictures literally stand out in three dimensions

explanation.walkthrough: Outstanding means excellent on the surface, but here it means standing out from the flat page in 3D.
explanation.definitionFit: These devices show each eye a slightly different photograph so the scene appears three-dimensional.

clue.text: The team won't be prepared to play without him

definitions.text: The team won't be prepared to play without him

parts.words: won't be prepared to play without him
parts.note: surface reading: players refusing to take the field unless a key member is there
setter's reading: the coach whose job is getting a side ready for matches

explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepared' sounds like willing, as if the team is sulking; it means made ready, which is this person's job.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach drills athletes and gets them fit, so without one a side would lack preparation.

clue.text: New part ordered in foreign port

indicators.note: things ordered are put into a sequence, so these letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A replacement part has been ordered from a supplier at an overseas harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: This Belgian city on the Scheldt is one of Europe's biggest harbours, foreign from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Miser and petty thief

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stingy person who hates spending
second meaning, taken literally: someone who pinches, or steals, small coins

explanation.walkthrough: To pinch is British slang for to steal, so the literal reading is a thief of small change.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a skinflint who counts every coin, and read literally it describes stealing small change.

clue.text: Wear and tear about target

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word is placed around the other

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip in cloth
an aim is a goal or target

explanation.surface: Clothes suffering wear and tear around a target area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wear and tear' reads as a single phrase, but it splits: the definition is the noun for clothing, and tear is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for clothing, which is what one puts on to wear.

clue.text: Ended series, having exceeded time allowed

parts.note: something finished is over
a run is a series, as in a run of wins

explanation.surface: A television series finished after going past its scheduled slot.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting or programme that has continued beyond its limit is said to have gone over schedule.

clue.text: Public minister about to return? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the combined letters read from right to left
this swaps the roles in the phrase before it, so the short word goes about the clergyman rather than inside him

parts.note: taken as written
short for Reverend, a minister's title

explanation.surface: A government minister about to come back into public view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite the opposite' swaps the roles: the short word goes about the minister, not inside him, and the whole is then turned back.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, in plain view rather than concealed, which is what public conveys.

clue.text: Move to the middle and compromise

definitions.meaning: first meaning, literal: travel half the distance
second meaning: meet the other side by conceding something

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means literally travel half the distance, and figuratively meet an opponent partway by conceding some ground.

clue.text: Restriction on movement, as worker strikes

parts.note: a hand is a labourer, as in farmhand
cuffs are blows with the open hand

explanation.surface: Industrial action limits movement of goods when the workforce strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikes' suggests industrial action, but here it means blows.
explanation.definitionFit: Police shackles lock a prisoner's wrists together, restraining the arms from moving freely.

clue.text: Burglar jokes with servant

parts.note: wisecracks, quips
a man is a manservant, as in 'my man'

explanation.surface: A housebreaker sharing a laugh with the butler.
explanation.definitionFit: This old term names a thief who breaks into houses or cracks open safes.

clue.text: Head off disaster and have a party with fruit

indicators.note: taking the head off a word removes its first letter

parts.note: havoc is devastation or chaos
taken as written
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Prevent a catastrophe and throw a celebration with some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off disaster' reads as prevent a catastrophe; instead the first letter is removed from the word for disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The pear-shaped tropical produce with a large stone is botanically a fruit, a berry in fact.

clue.text: A sign that trespassers aren't welcome

definitions.text: A sign that trespassers aren't welcome

parts.note: surface reading: an indication or hint of unfriendliness
setter's reading: the actual notice posted on private land

explanation.walkthrough: 'A sign that' reads like evidence of hostility; it is a literal noticeboard bearing the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Notices on private land carrying these words warn intruders not to step on the property.

clue.text: Canine tooth one has right in the centre

indicators.note: having something in the centre means another letter is placed in the middle of what came before

parts.note: a cog is a tooth on a gear wheel
the Roman numeral for one
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A canine tooth with a misalignment in the middle of the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine tooth' reads as one phrase, but canine is the definition and tooth starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A corgi is a short-legged Welsh breed of dog, famously kept by Queen Elizabeth II.

clue.text: A waterbed?

parts.note: surface reading: a mattress filled with water
setter's reading: the bed, or bottom, along which a stretch of water flows

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: not furniture but a bed of water, such as a riverbed or a strait.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a watercourse or strait whose bed carries flowing water, like the stretch between England and France.

clue.text: One in unusual stress doesn't give in

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other
something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters fall out of their normal order

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone under unusual pressure refuses to yield.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to withstand or hold out against pressure, refusing to yield or surrender.

clue.text: For one in ten it is essential to the diet

definitions.text: it is essential to the diet

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: in says the single letter is placed inside the number word

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A statistic claiming something is vital to the diet of one person in ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For one in ten' looks like a statistic; it splits into for, one and ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Protein builds and repairs body tissue, so nutritionists rank it among the vital nutrients in what we eat.

clue.text: Make a record score

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to tally by cutting marks
second meaning: a cut or nick, as scored in wood

explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a record score' reads as setting a new high; it splits into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallies were once kept by cutting nicks into a stick, so the verb means both to log and to incise.

clue.text: Top quality work produced by pupils in college, initially

parts.note: a class is a group of pupils

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words just before it

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A masterpiece created by students at a college.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic is a work of art or literature of acknowledged excellence that has stood the test of time.

clue.text: Main line terminal?

parts.note: surface reading: the end station of a principal railway route
setter's reading: the main is the sea, and this is where shipping lines end their voyages

explanation.walkthrough: The main is an old poetic word for the open sea, and a line is a shipping company.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour town where ships dock is the end point of routes across the ocean.

clue.text: It makes sense, if it is used to win at cards

definitions.text: it is used to win at cards

indicators.note: the answer is said to be made from the following letters, so they are rearranged to form it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tactic that seems sensible to use when trying to win a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge and whist this is a play that tries to win a trick with a lower card while a higher one is held.

clue.text: Few still show coarse male expressions

indicators.note: something coarse is rough and unrefined, so the letters are roughly reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Not many men still display crude behaviour these days.
explanation.definitionFit: These are whistles men aim at attractive women, a crude way of showing admiration.
